actions.name: conduct extensive pre-compromise reconnaissance
actions.description: Volt Typhoon conducts extensive pre-compromise reconnaissance to learn about the target organization’s network architecture, operational protocols, network topologies, security measures, typical user behaviors, and key network and IT staff.

actions.name: gain initial access by exploiting vulnerabilities in public-facing network appliances
actions.description: Volt Typhoon typically gains initial access to the IT network by exploiting known or zero-day vulnerabilities in public-facing network appliances such as routers, VPNs, and firewalls.

actions.name: connect to victim network via VPN for follow-on activities
actions.description: After initial access, Volt Typhoon actors connect to the victim’s network via VPN sessions to securely and discreetly conduct follow-on intrusion activities.

actions.name: obtain administrator credentials within the network
actions.description: Volt Typhoon aims to obtain administrator credentials within the network, often by exploiting privilege escalation vulnerabilities in the operating system or network services, or by obtaining credentials insecurely stored on public-facing network appliances.

actions.name: move laterally to domain controller and other devices via RDP using valid administrator credentials
actions.description: Volt Typhoon uses valid administrator credentials to move laterally to the domain controller and other devices via remote access services such as Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP).

actions.name: conduct discovery using LOTL binaries and PowerShell
actions.description: Volt Typhoon conducts discovery in the victim’s network, leveraging living off the land (LOTL) binaries for stealth, including using PowerShell to perform targeted queries on Windows event logs to extract security event logs into .dat files.

actions.name: extract Active Directory database (NTDS.dit) from domain controller using Volume Shadow Copy Service
actions.description: Volt Typhoon achieves full domain compromise by extracting the Active Directory database (NTDS.dit) from the domain controller, frequently employing the Volume Shadow Copy Service (VSS) using command-line utilities such as vssadmin to create a shadow copy and then copying NTDS.dit and SYSTEM registry hive from the volume shadow copy.

actions.name: exfiltrate NTDS.dit and SYSTEM registry hive for offline password cracking
actions.description: Volt Typhoon exfiltrates the extracted NTDS.dit and SYSTEM registry hive to perform offline password cracking to obtain plaintext passwords.

actions.name: use elevated credentials for strategic network infiltration and additional discovery
actions.description: Volt Typhoon uses elevated credentials obtained from NTDS.dit extraction to infiltrate the network further and conduct additional discovery, including testing access to OT assets using default OT vendor credentials and accessing OT systems.

actions.name: dump credentials from LSASS process memory using comsvcs.dll and MiniDump
actions.description: Volt Typhoon actors downloaded an outdated version of comsvcs.dll to a non-standard folder and used it with MiniDump and the process ID of LSASS to dump LSASS process memory and obtain credentials.

actions.name: use legitimate non-native network admin and forensic tools for credential harvesting
actions.description: Volt Typhoon actors have been observed using Magnet RAM Capture (MRC) to capture physical memory and likely analyze in-memory data for sensitive information such as credentials.

actions.name: use Mimikatz and Impacket for credential dumping and network protocol manipulation
actions.description: Volt Typhoon actors have been observed leveraging Mimikatz to harvest credentials and Impacket for Kerberos manipulation, credential dumping, packet sniffing, relay attacks, and remote service execution.

actions.name: exfiltrate sensitive information including OT equipment diagrams and documentation
actions.description: Volt Typhoon collected sensitive information from a file server in multiple zipped files and likely exfiltrated the files via SMB. The information included diagrams and documentation related to OT equipment such as SCADA systems, relays, and switchgear.

actions.name: implant and execute Fast Reverse Proxy (FRP) clients for command and control
actions.description: Volt Typhoon actors implanted FRP clients (BrightmetricAgent.exe and SMSvcService.exe) on victim servers and executed them via PowerShell to open reverse proxies between compromised systems and Volt Typhoon C2 servers, enabling covert communications.

actions.name: use netsh command to create PortProxy registry modification on PRTG server for C2 traffic proxying
actions.description: Volt Typhoon actors used the netsh command to create a PortProxy registry modification on a Paessler Router Traffic Grapher (PRTG) server, redirecting specific port traffic to Volt Typhoon’s proxy infrastructure and converting the PRTG server into a proxy for their C2 traffic.

relations.rationale: The source states the typical sequence starting with reconnaissance followed by initial access.
VPN connection is established after initial access using the foothold gained.
Obtaining administrator credentials depends on initial access to the network.
Lateral movement uses valid administrator credentials obtained earlier.
